description: MIKE IO is DHI's Python library for reading, writing and manipulating MIKE simulation files. It supports dfs0, dfs1, dfs2, dfs3, dfsu and mesh formats, organising values and geometry as Dataset and DataArray objects. The README demonstrates extracting a point time series, converting results to a Pandas data frame and writing a DFS file. Coverage, model resolution and dates come from the user's files, not a supplied geographic dataset. The source and package are publicly available and free under BSD-3-Clause. Current requirements specify 64-bit Python 3.12–3.14 on Windows or Linux, with additional Windows runtime components. A limitation is that the README says the conda-forge package is several major versions behind and recommends pip installation. The open I/O library does not provide a licence for commercial MIKE simulation engines. It helps prepare, inspect and compare hydraulic-model inputs and outputs, including work around the catalogue's MIKE+ platform (platform-dhi-mike-plus). The earlier candidate rejection considered it only a format utility; the current brief explicitly includes reusable data-preparation tools.
